newsitem.title: UK: Sell-off hits gold, copper steady.
newsitem.headline: Sell-off hits gold, copper steady.

text.p: Gold prices extended a slide on Friday to touch their lowest in almost 3-1/4 years as speculators marked the New Year with a vote of no confidence in bullion.

Investment funds selling gold in New York on Thursdasy had triggered the new decline. Bullion was fixed in London on Friday afternoon at $364.00 an ounce then was hit by new waves of selling that took it to a low bid of $361.80. Gold had ended 1996 at almost $368. It is now at its weakest since October 1993. One London trader spoke of "gold's bearish internal combustion" after speculators late in 1996 lost patience with it and began to bale out. Fears that some European central banks might sell gold holdings to raise money to meet economic criteria for European monetary union dogged the market in December.
Other commodity markets were subdued after the Christmas and New Year holidays in the West and because of a holiday in Japan. Acitivity may begin to pick up on Monday.
London Metal Exchange three months copper futures extended a modest advance to trade at $2,208 per tonne after ending 1996 at $2,127.
Copper later eased to just under $2,200 on end-week book squaring but some traders expect to see the rally continue if it can hold above $2,175. The price has firmed because of low stocks.
Benchmark Brent Blend crude oil futures eased just below $24 per barrel despite cold weather on profit-taking after news of a rise in U.S. heating oil stocks.
The American Petroleum Institute said U.S. distillates stocks in the week to December 27 rose 2.47 million barrels.
